summary:
--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "GENERAL COOPERATION ADVICE. This is general guidance, not a measurement or diagnosis of this parent." and "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that defects in the last 3 rounds and detects always-defect/always-cooperate. The trace simulates the 12 population opponents and their payoffs, and considers adding opponent modeling, probing, and exploitation of always-cooperate. No change has been made yet in this part; it is still analyzing and designing an improved strategy.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice strongly emphasizes forgiveness and maintaining cooperation. So we should not probe aggressively."
STRATEGY: Parent is a cautious retaliatory strategy that cooperates, retaliates after opponent defection, and defects near the end. The trace simulates probing/exploiting always-C opponents and TFT-with-forgiveness variants against the 12 listed opponents. It considers changing to a more forgiving strategy, limiting probing, and adjusting endgame defection length.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice emphasizes cooperation. So I'll lean towards a very forgiving strategy that only defects in the last 1-2 rounds"
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving Tit-for-Tat with endgame defection (last 3 rounds) and some retaliation logic; the trace simulates probing/defecting against always-C, TFT, and the 12 population opponents to test exploitation and forgiveness; it proposes a more forgiving TFT that probes early, exploits non-retaliators, and defects in the last 5 rounds.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the general advice and the fact that the population is mostly cooperative, a very forgiving strategy that only retaliates if opponent defects twice in a row, and then forgives immediately, might be best."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, retaliates after opponent defection, and apologizes after mutual defection. The trace simulates probing/exploitation against always-cooperative and retaliatory opponents, then revises toward a forgiving Tit-for-Tat with early probing and endgame defection.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So this strategy seems robust and likely improves over parent."
STRATEGY: Parent defects only in the last 3 rounds and retaliates more; simulated against always-D, always-C, occasional defectors, and retaliators; changed to exploit never-defecting opponents from round 5, add an 80% defection-rate defense, and apologize after mutual defection.
